definition: Phi is a series of large language models developed by Microsoft that are open-weights and can run locally on one's device.
details: The initial version, Phi-1, released in June 2023. Phi-3 was released in April 2024. Phi-4-reasoning-vision-15B was released in March 2026. The New York Times considered Phi-3-mini to be Microsoft's push into smaller large language models. Phi-3-mini has 3.8 billion parameters. Phi-3-mini has been compared to GPT-3.5 in terms of capability.

explainer.lead: Phi is Microsoft's series of open-weights large language models designed to run locally on a single device. It matters as evidence that small models can rival much larger ones in capability.

tiers.eli5: These are AI models small enough to live on your own computer instead of a big data centre, yet still fairly capable.
tiers.practitioner: Use Phi when you need an on-device model with downloadable weights. Pitfall: a 3.8B-parameter model like Phi-3-mini, compared to GPT-3.5 in capability, is still a small model, so expect it to fall short on the heaviest tasks.
tiers.paperLevel: A family of open-weights transformer language models; Phi-1 appeared June 2023, Phi-3 April 2024, Phi-4-reasoning-vision-15B March 2026. Phi-3-mini has 3.8 billion parameters; capability is bounded by that scale.

explainer.example: A developer downloads Phi-3-mini (3.8B parameters) and runs it offline on a laptop for local text generation.
